rules.title: Search crawler that powers AI answers is blocked
rules.description: Googlebot or Bingbot is blocked. Google AI Overviews/AI Mode use pages from the Google Search index, and Bing Copilot grounds answers on Bing-indexed pages; blocking these crawlers removes the site from both classic and AI search.
rules.fix: Allow Googlebot/Bingbot for public content. Use nosnippet/max-snippet or the Search Console generative AI setting to limit AI use instead.
rules.verify: Re-test robots.txt for Googlebot and Bingbot.

sources.title: Google: AI features and your website

rules.title: AI search crawler blocked
rules.description: A crawler that builds an AI search index (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot) is disallowed. Per the operators' documentation, blocked sites may not appear (or appear only as links) in that product's search answers.
rules.fix: If you want visibility in that AI search product, allow its search crawler. Training crawlers can be blocked independently.
rules.verify: Re-test robots.txt for the bot token.

sources.title: Anthropic: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web

rules.exceptions: Intentional blocking is a business decision; Searvex reports, it does not judge.

rules.title: AI training crawler access summary
rules.description: Status of crawlers/tokens used for model training (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, Meta-ExternalAgent). Blocking them does not affect classic search or (for Google-Extended) AI Overviews inclusion.
rules.fix: Decide per operator; blocking training does not require blocking search crawlers.

sources.title: Anthropic: Does Anthropic crawl data from the web

rules.title: Snippet controls limit AI feature usage
rules.description: nosnippet / max-snippet:0 (Google) or noarchive / nocache (Bing) restrict how content can be shown in AI Overviews/AI Mode and Copilot answers. Listed for review; may be intentional.
rules.fix: Remove the restriction on pages you want quoted in AI answers; keep it where you need control.

Bing: Options to control content usage in Bing Chat (NOARCHIVE/NOCACHE)

rules.title: llms.txt status (informational)
rules.description: Reports whether /llms.txt exists. It is a 2024 proposal, not a standard; Google documents that it does not use it for Search or AI features, and no major search engine documents consuming it. Its presence or absence is not scored.
rules.fix: No action required for search visibility.

rules.title: Inconsistent organisation name across pages
rules.description: Organization/WebSite names in structured data or og:site_name differ across pages. Consistent naming helps search engines and AI systems resolve the brand as one entity (Google uses WebSite name and Organization data for site names).
rules.fix: Use one canonical brand name in Organization/WebSite markup and og:site_name.

sources.title: Google: Site names in Google Search

rules.title: Content structure review for answerability
rules.description: Heuristic signals of how easily a page's answers can be extracted: descriptive headings, concise paragraphs following question-style headings, lists/tables, and visible dates/authors. Google states no special optimisation is required for AI features; these are general clarity signals, not ranking or citation predictors.
rules.fix: Write clear, people-first content: descriptive headings, direct answers near the top of sections, cited sources.

sources.title: Google: Creating helpful, reliable, people-first content

rules.title: AI citations not measured
rules.description: Searvex cannot observe whether AI systems cite this site without a platform integration. Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance (preview) and the Search Console generative AI performance data are the official sources.
rules.fix: Export Bing AI Performance data or Search Console data and import it (searvex monitor --import).
